content:
Hi, Just been playing around with lean proofs and I think I have an Independence of the Parallel Postulate lean proof.
Source available here: https://github.com/Richiesutie/ParallelPostulate
Please note, this was almost entirely written by AI, with my only main contribution being setting up the initial definitions for the dimensions.
Hello, can you elaborate on why Hilbert's axioms instead of Tarski's axioms? (as the other solutions on Freek's list use)
Hi Snir, at the time I wasn't aware of the other solutions, would it be better to swap to tarskis to keep in line with the other solutions? i'm not sure on the etiquette for posting lean proofs.

I think both are interesting; it depends on what your goals are with your project. Are you trying to learn Lean, or contribute to Mathlib, or create your own projects with AI, or complete Freek's list, etc?
But even ignoring the other solutions, is there a reason behind the choice of Hilbert instead of Tarski?

Apologies if this is a bit rude, but since you asked about etiquette- IMO it went out the window as this is AI authored. But opinions vary (even among the mods of this Zulip I think). You can see in the community guidelines the sentence

Posts that amount to 'look at my project' without a specific question or prior community involvement will be removed and the poster suspended.

which I think applies here, although nowadays this is not usually enforced and there are tons of such posts. I think that by disclosing AI usage and writing the post yourself you've done better than most :)

I think my main goal here was seeing how far ai had improved with mathematics. The last time I tried this was a few years and it constantly hallucinated.

I did some minor research into why the proof is not in Mathlib already, and the reason as I understand is the lack of unification between the two proofs for Euclidean and hyperbolic. With this project both models come from a single construction with a curvature parameter κ, so the same proofs cover both. κ = 0 gives the Euclidean plane and κ = −1 gives the Klein model of the hyperbolic plane.

Behind the reason for Hilbert. As I understand it, Hilbert axioms are closer to Euclid and is more the natural fit.

Not rude at all, and apologies. Having glanced through the guidelines I thought it best to share this only in the new members channel and see the response. I would understand if this got deleted.
This topic was moved here from #new members > Richard Sutton -Independence Parallel Postulate by Michael Rothgang.

Back in 2003, Meikle and Fleuriot formalized Hilbert's Grundlagen in Isabelle/Isar. That would be one reason to use Hilbert's axioms, if one were specifically interested in the Grundlagen. By the way, Meikle and Fleuriot claimed that their formalization revealed that even Hilbert sometimes glossed over steps that were "obvious" from a diagram, but which strictly speaking required proof.
